claim.summary: For fixed binary old inputs of degree<=delta in a Boolean PC pseudoideal J_D, original accuracy h, coefficient bound T>=1 and common binary coefficient basis, suppose degree<=b weights W_j have successful maps with row spaces R_j. If k=dim(sum R_j)<=h and b+TB<=D for B>=max(2,h(delta+1)+delta), a padded basis of the union is one map successful at every W_j and their binary linear combinations. Row reduction, extending bases by factors and paid row invariance retain original h and B; number of witnesses does not enter the degree. No survival, union-dimension bound, or source-wide varying-weight reconstruction is asserted.
claim.assessment: Working paid composition of the row-gauge lemma, passed by one fresh medium reviewer with adaptive-versus-uniform scope clarified.

claim.summary: For all h,T>=1, r=h(T+1)+1 independent Boolean input bits, accuracy h, all binary coefficient maps of degree<=T (also allowing additional old bits), and Boolean-only J_D with D>=1+T(2h+1): every homogeneous linear weight has an adaptive successful map but no single permitted map serves that whole linear space; moreover x_1 and 1+x_1 are feasible surviving weights while their sum 1 is infeasible. The complement weight uses h packed groups of T+1 inputs; unit-weight failure follows from forced degree-r zero-test versus product degree<=r-1. Weighted field certificates fit. This is a consistent Boolean-cube control, not a charged hard-quotient obstruction.
claim.assessment: Working all-parameter adaptive-weight control passed by one fresh medium reviewer; uses existing packing and the pointwise degree barrier, retaining the full degree-bounded coefficient domain and Boolean-only scope.

claim.summary: For an acyclic binary product-only ENS source with degree<=T binary coefficient maps in identical row spaces, original s_a=h_a(delta_a+1), B>=max(2,max_a(s_a+delta_a)) and b+TB<=D, independent invertible binary constant row operations in each block preserve all weighted product and companion classes in the old Boolean pseudoideal, after coherent rebuilding. Elementary row addition changes the product by (A^2+A) times other factors, certified through Ts_a; descendant telescoping pays original expression weights. Thus successful maps have reduced-row-echelon coefficient matrices at the same degree and original accuracy. Rank/pivot patterns define affine binary gauges covering geometric existence at b+T max(B,3L)<=D after descent; no success is asserted for a particular pattern or for nonbinary row maps.
claim.assessment: Working costed source-wide Boolean row-invariance proof passed by one fresh medium reviewer, with the combined geometric-cover ceiling clarified and rechecked; includes a nonbinary countercontrol.

claim.summary: For h>=2,T>=1,r=h(T+1) independent Boolean inputs, a complete accuracy-h block with row coefficients of degree<=T in those variables over the Boolean-only base through D>=T(2h+1) has successful maps but zero full coefficient of its identical-row-grid success indicator. One active row cannot realize the degree-r zero-test. Historical factor packing gives an asymmetric affine h-bit parameter chart tau_u, controlling each group's last coefficient, on which success is exactly product tau_u and the full coefficient is one. Companion degree r+1 and field degree2T fit the original replay ceiling.
claim.assessment: Reviewed explicit application of historical packing and pointwise barrier, not a new packing theorem or a hard-family lower bound. The source base is a consistent Boolean cube; the successful construction is known before the chart is made.
